2.measure_note: Landscape sheet rendered portrait, so ROW bands are rowbands.py's v_rules_pct and the AMOUNT column band comes from h_rules_pct; rows advance from HIGH x to LOW x (row 1 is the highest band). Detected v_rules had constant pitch ~3.06 and needed no extrapolation. Trimmed the two non-data bands at the head of the table before index-aligning: the 'Amount' HEADER band [85.06,90.05] and the shaded/hatched spacer band [81.94,85.06] (addendum 2026-08-18 §2.2) -- leaving them in would have pointed every row one or two rows early. cell = the AMOUNT column, which is the LAST column of the printed table; its band [86.10,96.81] was taken from the two printed column rules (h_rules 86.10 and the table's bottom border 96.81) and was confirmed by a full-height crop of row band 1, which rendered the whole row 2/14/2014 | 4Imprint | online | Promotional Materials | 326.21 with the figure sitting inside 86.10-96.81. deskew_deg 0.3 so bands were treated as provisional and settled by crop. PROOF (900 dpi --value): first row pct:78.86,86.10,3.08,10.71@p2 rendered '326.21' (recorded 326.21); last row pct:63.48,86.10,3.08,10.71@p2 rendered '150.00' (recorded 150.00). 'cells' is deliberately OMITTED: only the amount column's two bounding rules were crop-verified, and the interior column boundaries were estimated rather than measured -- an estimate is not written as a measurement.
